narr: A midlevel shortwave trough was situated over the Upper Midwest Sunday night (31st) into Monday morning (1st). At the surface, a strong occluded low was also present. From this low and occlusion, a warm front extended to the southeast, lifting through the Commonwealth during the same time frame. A MCS developed in the Upper Mississippi Valley and continued to push southeast towards the Commonwealth during the morning hours. This prompted SPC to put portions of northern and eastern KY in a slight risk for severe weather throughout the day. Ironically, we did not see any severe weather out of this system - however, showers that developed during the morning hours ahead of the MCS were a different story. These showers developed over the eastern portion of the state, and impacted areas that were already heavily saturated from the devastating rains that occurred the week before. More so, the convection was moving parallel to the mean flow, which meant that many of these showers continued to train over the same locations for an extended period of time. This prompted flash flood warnings, and led to impacts in Martin, Pike, Letcher, Floyd, and Knott counties.
ev: Media reports water flowing over Big Branch Ball Road near the community of Emmalena.
Water was reported on the road in several locations along KY-550 in Hindman.
Water was over the road on the creek-side of Abbott Creek Rd near Bonanza.
Ruff and Tuff Road culvert was washed out, leading to the road being closed near the community of Dotson.
Water was reported out of the banks along Lower Dix Fork near the Canada community and getting into nearby homes.
Water was ponding onto the KY-2759 near Hindman. In addition, a mudslide also occurred, and a large tree is down. Power lines are also down in the area as a result. The road has been been closed.

Pictures show King's Collision (NAPA store) in Neon surrounded by flash flood waters. The waters were up to the floor of a vehicle in the parking lot. The media also reported flash flooding on the streets at the intersection of KY-317 and KY-343 just past King's Collision.
